correctness.rationale: Maximal-source successor sets force the last source antichain into the target top. A nonsingleton top target antichain must be covered wholly by this last level, inducing a bijection with a lower-prefix p-morphism and an ordinary surjection. A singleton top target instead yields a unique last non-top source level and a nonempty subset of it; restricting to the lower target and reversing this extension are inverse. The terminal-subset state is therefore exact, with all boundary cases addressed. Inclusion-exclusion proves the S and T weights; a separately implemented exhaustive set-function test matches 687 profile pairs, corroborating but not replacing the symbolic proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The previous all-map and homotopy theorems do not logically yield the displayed formula without new analysis of the back condition. In particular, W(1,3,1) admits an onto monotone map to W(1,2,1) sending a middle source point to the target bottom, the other two middle source points onto both target middle points and the last point to the target top; its middle-bottom source point has no successor mapping to a target middle point, so the surjective map violates the back property. The present last-non-top-level bijection is necessary to handle singleton target gates. Huczynska--Ruškuc is a plausible related source whose unavailable full manuscript leaves a specific, disclosed residual comparison risk, not demonstrated stronger coverage.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparisons with Kupke--Pattinson and three strongly related published weak-order mapping results reveal no exact cardinality theorem for the stricter onto bounded-morphism class. The closest all-map theorem does not imply the new back-condition enumeration by specialization, and the closest homotopy theorem counts different objects and excludes singleton gates. published-finding corpus and literature alias searches found no stronger coverage. The inaccessible surjective-homomorphism manuscript and potentially unindexed equivalent formulations remain explicit risks.
residual_risks: Full text of Huczynska--Ruškuc could not be inspected; an exact p-morphism enumeration hidden there cannot be ruled out, although its abstract addresses different order-theoretic questions.
Unindexed literature might express the same count via coalgebra homomorphisms, modal frame quotients or Heyting-algebra duality.
Published weak-order homotopy formulas coincide with the onto function factor for binary target antichains; those special cases are not claimed separately as new.

value.rationale: Surjective bounded morphisms are semantically natural finite-frame quotients that preserve and reflect the accessibility successor structure. For arbitrary weak-order level vectors, the count reduces from exponential set-map testing to two coupled dynamic-programming tables. The dichotomy between terminal target antichains of size at least two and singleton gates is a structural phenomenon, not a routine parameter substitution. It covers unbounded heights and arbitrarily many interspersed singleton levels; it supplies a reusable exact answer where existing general map counts and homotopy classifications do not.
